name: GIA diamond cut grade (round brilliant)
steps: Excellent > Poor
notes: page names only the endpoints of the relative scale; intermediate grades not on the fetched page; applies to standard round brilliants in the D-to-Z range

name: GIA coloured diamond colour grades
steps: Fancy Deep > Fancy Dark > Fancy Vivid > Fancy Intense > Fancy > Fancy Light > Light > Very Light > Faint
notes: page lists the grades in order of increasing colour strength (Faint to Fancy Deep) and puts Fancy Dark before Fancy Deep without explaining their relative strength; listed here reversed

name: GIA pearl luster grades (one of seven value factors)
steps: Excellent > Very Good > Good > Fair > Poor
notes: seven value factors in page order: size, shape, color, luster, surface quality, nacre quality, matching (jewelry with two or more pearls); page says luster might be the most important

name: Mineral specimen size classes
steps: Very large cabinet > Large cabinet > Cabinet > Small cabinet > Miniature > Thumbnail > Micromount
notes: Mikon table in inches: micromount up to 1 in (25 mm), miniature 1.6-2 in (41-51 mm), small cabinet 3-3.5 in (76-89 mm), cabinet 4.5-6 in (114-152 mm), large cabinet 8-12 in (203-305 mm), very large cabinet above; iRocks: thumbnail usually no larger than 1 in square, toenail informal between thumbnail and miniature; table is for orientation only

name: U.S. beef quality grades
steps: Prime > Choice > Select > Standard > Commercial > Utility > Cutter > Canner
notes: Prime at least slightly abundant marbling, Choice at least Small, Select at least Slight; Standard and Commercial often sold ungraded; Utility, Cutter, Canner go to ground and processed beef

name: Japan beef carcass yield grades (歩留等級)
steps: A > B > C
notes: Yield standard value 72 or above is A, 69 to under 72 is B, under 69 is C

name: Japan beef carcass quality grades (肉質等級)
notes: Set by four items (marbling, colour and brightness, firmness and texture, fat colour and quality); the carcass takes the lowest of the four item grades; marbling bands 5 = BMS 8-12, 4 = 5-7, 3 = 3-4, 2 = 2, 1 = 1; combined with yield grade as A5, B4 etc.

name: Beef Marbling Standard (BMS No. 1-12)
notes: Marbling of the longissimus thoracis judged against photo standards; page maps No.8-12 to quality 5, 5-7 to 4, 3-4 to 3, 2 to 2, 1 to 1 and does not describe each of the 12 steps

name: Korea beef quality grades (육질등급)
owner: Korea Institute for Animal Products Quality Evaluation
notes: Preliminary grade from marbling, then meat colour, fat colour, texture and maturity; page covers domestic beef in general and does not separate Hanwoo

name: Korea beef yield grades (육량등급)
owner: Korea Institute for Animal Products Quality Evaluation
steps: A > B > C
notes: From back-fat thickness, ribeye area and carcass weight by a yield formula; numeric cut-offs not on the page

name: Ibérico sale denominations and colour seals (Real Decreto 4/2014)
steps: Black seal: de bellota 100% ibérico > Red seal: de bellota ibérico > Green seal: de cebo de campo ibérico > White seal: de cebo ibérico
notes: Feeding term (de bellota, de cebo de campo, de cebo) plus breed term (100% ibérico, ibérico at least 50% Iberian genetics); seal per Art. 9.3, cured loin follows Art. 9.5; a label class, never a named form

name: EU poultrymeat farming-type terms (Regulation 543/2008 Annex V)
steps: Free range - total freedom > Traditional free range > Free range > Extensive indoor (barn-reared)
notes: Text read from the legislation.gov.uk copy of the EU regulation as at 1 July 2022; later EU amendments not checked; slaughter ages and stocking limits differ by term (for example chicken minimum 56 days extensive indoor, 81 days traditional free range)

name: Global Animal Partnership 5-Step animal welfare steps
steps: Step 5+: Animal centered, entire life on same farm > Step 5: Animal centered, no physical alterations > Step 4: Pasture centered > Step 2: Enriched environment > Step 1: No crowding
notes: Labels read from the beef cattle standard v1.2 (2022); that standard has no Step 3 and other species may show a Step 3 not seen here

name: EU olive oil and olive-pomace oil categories
steps: Extra-virgin olive oil > Virgin olive oil > Olive oil composed of refined and virgin olive oils > Olive-pomace oil (refined, blended with virgin)
notes: Extra-virgin acidity not above 0.8%, virgin not above 2%, refined-plus-virgin blend not above 1%; virgin lampante, refined olive oil and crude pomace oil are not for retail; page does not cite Regulation 2022/2104 text

name: UMF manuka honey grades
steps: UMF 25+ > UMF 20+ > UMF 15+ > UMF 10+ > UMF 5+
notes: Each grade sets minimum MGO, leptosperin, DHA and HMF limits (UMF 5+ MGO 83, 10+ 261, 15+ 512, 20+ 826, 25+ 1197 mg/kg); page says MGO ratings do not convert to UMF so no separate MGO grade row

name: U.S. grades of shelled almonds
steps: U.S. Fancy > U.S. Extra No. 1 > U.S. No. 1 > U.S. Select Sheller Run > U.S. Standard Sheller Run > U.S. No. 1 Whole and Broken > U.S. No. 1 Pieces
notes: Order as listed on the page; grades differ by tolerances for doubles, chipped kernels and defects

name: U.S. grades of shelled walnuts
steps: U.S. No. 1 > U.S. Commercial
notes: Colour (extra light to amber, or red) and size are specified with the grade

name: U.S. grades of walnuts in the shell
steps: U.S. No. 1 > U.S. No. 2 > U.S. No. 3
notes: Kernel colour and share of light kernels vary by grade; pecan and other nut standards not fetched

name: Japan rice taste ranking (米の食味ランキング)
steps: 特A > A > A' > B > B'
notes: Panel tasting of cooked rice against a blended Koshihikari reference, by area and cultivar each crop year; 2025 crop: 43 Toku-A, 71 A, 30 A', none B or B' of 144 entries

name: ICCO fine or flavour cocoa class
steps: Fine or flavour cocoa > Bulk (ordinary) cocoa
notes: Provisional; a country-level share list under the International Cocoa Agreement 2010 Annex C, Council decision April 2024 (for example Ecuador and Peru 75%, Colombia 80%, Grenada 100%); no single criterion for fine flavour
